The tornado moved in a northwest to southeast direction and was located near Johnny Creek. The tornado was 100 yards wide, 3/4 of a mile long, and was on the ground for approximately 5 minutes. The tornado remained over open range while on the ground and caused no property damage. F1 tornadoes produce wind speeds from 73 to 112 mph.

ncei:5133907.title: Nashville, Tennessee
ncei:5133907.narrative: About 50 homes and 20 businesses received damage from this tornado.  A 25 foot hackberry tree fell on a house.  An oak tree crashed into the side of a building. A school trailer was destroyed at St. Vincent De Paul School. There was 15 rooftop damage  at an apartment complex on Delta Street.  The hardest hit area of downtown Nashville was the Eight Avenue North and Bordeaux .  The tornado started around Scovel Street and 28th Avenue North. Extensive damage occurred from this location and to the eastnortheast for just over a mile in length. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. Powerlines were down. A number of homes suffered roof damage. The tornado crossed I-265 , moving eastnortheast reaching Arthur Avenue, 10th Ave. and 9th Ave. North, crossed the Cumberland River  and then reaching Dickerson Pike and Ellington Parkway, finally dissipating around Petway Avenue and Gallatin Road.One woman was injured when an interstate sign blew into her car and caused her  to wreck.

ncei:5136873.title: Eagleville, Tennessee
ncei:5136873.narrative: TEMA confirmed report of a tornado. The tornado did no damage.

ncei:5157965.title: North Port, Florida
ncei:5157965.narrative: A short lived tornado, that originated in Charlotte county and was associated with an outer rainband of Hurricane Gordon, briefly touched down, snapped a few trees, downed power lines and damaged a few carports, east of the intersection of Interstate 75 and Toledo Blade Boulevard.  The tornado continued to sporadically touch down along a narrow path as it moved rapidly north across Interstate 75 over rural southeast Sarasota county before it lifted and dissipated.

ncei:5158879.title: Waukeenah, Florida
ncei:5158879.narrative: Two mobile homes were damaged by a brief F0 tornado.  Reported by the Jefferson County EMA.

ncei:5160314.title: Elgin, Texas
ncei:5160314.narrative: A small and short-lived tornado was observed by the public near Elgin.  It caused no damage.

ncei:5162781.title: Clam Falls, Wisconsin
ncei:5162781.narrative: Touched down in open field, no damage incurred. Tornado originally touched down in Burnett county, from 1735-1740.

ncei:5168219.title: Abbeville, Alabama
ncei:5168219.narrative: The F2 tornado continued its intermittent track northeast from eastern Dale County into western Henry County, but had weakened to an F1 tornado.  Just north of Murphy Station along Highway 27 and a quarter mile west of U.S. Highway 431, the tornado completely destroyed the Murphy Feed & Seed warehouse, numerous peanut trailers and two sheds.  Before the tornado dissipated, it severely damaged the West Point Stevens Textile plant.  Numerous vehicles were damaged.  Henry County was declared a federal disaster area.  Reported by the Henry County EMA.

ncei:5679136.title: Muscle Shoals, Alabama
ncei:5679136.narrative: A tornado briefly touched down 5 miles south of Muscle Shoals with little or no damage. The tornado was also reported on the Muscle Shoals surface observation at 1543 through 1557.  Emergency management surveyed the area of the tornado report and could not find any damage in a mostly open area.

ncei:5689960.title: Hattiesburg, Mississippi
ncei:5689960.narrative: This weak tornado touched down in Hattiesburg with no damage reported.

ncei:5693068.title: Alliance, Louisiana
ncei:5693068.narrative: A tornado briefly touched one half mile north of Alliance and just north of the British Petroleum Refinery.  The tornado lifted a mobile home off of its foundation and set it back down, blew a cinder block through the wall of another mobile home, destroyed a greenhouse, and blew a shed across Highway 23.

ncei:5697445.title: Wink, Texas
ncei:5697445.narrative: Brief tornado that became rain-wrapped very quickly.  Brief glimpse of large cone-shaped funnel.

ncei:5705300.title: Minco, Oklahoma
ncei:5705300.narrative: Tornado B8. See summary at end of May 3rd storm reports.

ncei:5705621.title: Mulhall, Oklahoma
ncei:5705621.narrative: Tornado G6. See summary at end of May 3rd storm reports.

ncei:5636648.title: St George, South Carolina
ncei:5636648.narrative: Roof on brick home damaged, shed destroyed , a boat was thrown 40 feet and a couple of trees were uprooted.

ncei:5636651.title: St Stephen, South Carolina
ncei:5636651.narrative: Several trees and limbs down, mobile home damaged, minor roof damage to several brick homes and outdoor shed destroyed.

ncei:5643738.title: Cypress, Illinois
ncei:5643738.narrative: A short-lived tornado began along the Union County line, just southwest of Cypress, and tracked east along a rural road before dissipating at State Route 37. A small barn, about 150 square feet in area, was blown across the road. Some pieces of wood were stuck in the ground at an angle up to 200 feet away. One house sustained siding damage. Another house had a portion of its roof lifted up and placed back down again. A bedroom in the house was damaged. In addition, very minor damage occurred to a greenhouse, an abandoned house, and a couple of mobile homes. Trees, power lines, and power poles were down along the path of the tornado. Large trees, two feet in diameter, were blown down in between two mobile homes. Along Route 37, six power poles were snapped off about two feet above the ground. A female motorist was injured when her moving vehicle was struck by a falling tree. She was treated and released from a local hospital for minor injuries. Just north of Cypress, several large trees were down, but this damage was likely due to straight-line thunderstorm winds.

ncei:5664633.title: Andersonville, Georgia
ncei:5664633.narrative: A newspaper report indicated another brief touchdown by an apparent tornado took out a pecan grove on Georgia highway 49 near Andersonville. This would probably have been from the same storm that had hit near DeSoto about 35 minutes earlier.

ncei:5598930.title: Utopia, Texas
ncei:5598930.narrative: Amateur Radio spotters relayed a report of a tornado sighted by a Sheriff's Deputy.

ncei:5600397.title: Tacoma, Washington
ncei:5600397.narrative: A weak tornado touched down in a south Tacoma neighborhood just east of I-5.  A church suffered roof and beam damage and several trees were pushed over or snapped off.  There were also some downed fences.

ncei:5612333.title: Mercer, North Dakota
ncei:5612333.narrative: brief touchdown by a rope tornado in open county.

ncei:5582081.title: Linden, Pennsylvania
ncei:5582081.narrative: This storm was a continuation of damage that occurred in the Avis and Jersey Shore areas. The tornado caused intermittent damage along a 2.5 mile path in Woodward Township northwest of Linden. The tornado tore a brick facade off the southeast face of the Lycoming Christian Church at the initial touchdown northwest of Linden, then moved east northeast taking down trees in spots and doing minor damage to a couple of homes and a shed along the 2.5 mile path.

ncei:10318322.title: Kersey, Colorado
ncei:10318322.narrative: A tornado was on the ground for 30 seconds in an open field.

ncei:10321919.title: Milton, Indiana
ncei:10321919.narrative: A tornado touched down near Indiana State Route One, damaging a 40- by 120-foot barn.  The tornado also downed several trees and power lines.

ncei:10328230.title: Edmonton, Kentucky
ncei:10328230.narrative: Tornado touched down in Edmonton then traveled along U.S. 80 to the Adair County line 14 miles to the West.  A mobile and three barns were destroyed.  Several homes and a factory were damaged.  Many trees and power lines were also blown down.

ncei:10353958.title: Near Woodlands, Texas
ncei:10353958.narrative: Tornado briefly touched down east of the Woodlands killing one horse and doing minor damage to barn.

ncei:10333995.title: Central City, Nebraska
ncei:10333995.narrative: A tornado touched down near the Platte River three miles south of Central City and then moved north to the east edge of town where it lifted back into the clouds.  Outbuildings were damaged and tree tops were twisted off at three separate farms.  The tornado blew the roof off of an auto body shop on the east edge of town.

ncei:10338315.title: Statesville, North Carolina
ncei:10338315.narrative: Six mobile homes were damaged.  A wall was blown down at a home under construction.  Trees and power lines were damaged.

ncei:10318598.title: Huerfano, Colorado
ncei:10318598.narrative: A tornado developed two miles southwest of the town of La Veta and moved north to two miles west of La Veta before dissipating.  The tornado touched down periodically along its track.  Two barns were destroyed and at least 20 pine and cottonwood trees (up to 100 feet tall) were uprooted.  Downed trees had to be removed from several roads.  Estimates placed damages at $100,000.  There were no deaths or injuries.

ncei:10320309.title: Atwater, Illinois
ncei:10320309.narrative: A tornado briefly touched down in a cornfield 1 mile north of Atwater, causing extensive damage to the crop.  No crop damage estimate was available.

ncei:10328283.title: New Iberia, Louisiana
ncei:10328283.narrative: The Iberia Parish emergency manager said a small, brief tornado occurred in an open field about 3 miles northeast of New Iberia about 1500 CST.

ncei:10350366.title: Keene, Texas
ncei:10350366.narrative: A brief tornado touchdown occurred between Keene and Alvarado.
